subject: Request: temporary tranche shift for LumenRx pilot (autoscale exception + reservation ask)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary tranche shift for LumenRx pilot (autoscale exception + reservation ask)

Team — quick heads-up and ask from the field. LumenRx is ramping a 3-week enterprise pilot starting Nov 29 that will run sustained QA + integration loadtests for their real-time charting workflow. They need consistent sub-120ms tail latency for inference checks during test windows (14:00–18:00 PT daily).

Current ask from Sales/Customer: can we shift a 12-GPU tranche from the general dev pool into a short-term reserved lane for the pilot (Nov 29–Dec 19) and grant an autoscale soft-exemption that prevents aggressive preemption during the 14:00–18:00 window? They understand this is conditional and are open to compensating burn.

What I need from Product/Capacity: 1) feasibility on carving a dedicated tranche without materially impacting queued pilots, 2) recommended configuration (pool assignment, soft SLOs, fallback model variant), and 3) a short runbook snippet we can send the customer for expected failure/fallback behavior.

Attached: tranche_realloc_plan_v2.xlsx (rough impact calc) and estimated_burn_vs_slo.png.

Proposed compromise I heard from Solutions: make it a scheduled reserved lane during local business hours (14:00–18:00 PT) only, and require the customer to use the q3-lowmem quantized model for stress windows to reduce slot usage.

Goal: firm answer by EOD Thursday (Nov 18) so Sales can confirm SOW tempo.

— Stephanie
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary tranche shift for LumenRx pilot (autoscale exception + reservation ask)

Thanks Steph — good summary. Quick notes from Capacity/Operations POV:

- A full 12-GPU carve is heavy; we should consider a time-sliced reservation: reserve 6 GPUs exclusively 14:00–18:00 PT and allow burst to 12 GPUs subject to preemption outside the window. That reduces churn to the general pool.
- Autoscale soft-exemption: we can implement a soft-preemption policy (lower eviction score) during the 4-hour window for that tranche, but we need an approval from Product since it alters fairness scoring.
- Impact: roughly 8–12% increased latency risk for queued pilot workloads in the same shard during that window (see attached). If we accept the q3-lowmem variant it cuts memory by ~30% which helps packing.

Action items I need from Product: recommended fallback model (latency vs quality tradeoff), and Product sign-off to special-case fairness scoring for this tranche during the time window.

— Kim
Head of Dedicated Capacity

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 09:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary tranche shift for LumenRx pilot (autoscale exception + reservation ask)

Stephanie / Kim — product questions and risks:

- Fallback model: recommend q3-llm-small-quant (artifact: model-v2q-small). It preserves NLU fidelity for the chart checks while trimming memory and tokens per second cost. Latency penalty is <8% in our bench runs.
- Fairness scoring exception: acceptable as a one-off if we codify it (time-boxed, Tier-2 review) and log events for audit. We should require customer to accept a higher SOA (SLA amendment stub) for guaranteed reserved lane.
- Monitoring: add a temporary SLO target in Console for that tranche and enable token-level cost tracking — this will help bill-back in near-real-time.

I'll draft the SLO amendment and a fallback behavioral paragraph for the runbook.

— Laura
Product Manager, Serving

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2027 14:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary tranche shift for LumenRx pilot (autoscale exception + reservation ask)

I agree with the time-sliced approach. A couple of operational constraints to flag to Sales so they set expectations with LumenRx:

1) We cannot guarantee uninterrupted capacity beyond the 4-hour scheduled window; outside that window the tranche will fall back to shared pool.
2) If we mark the tranche with a lower eviction score, other high-priority customers may see higher preemption. We'll need CS/Account to sign a temporary amendment that includes a charge for dedicated time and a clause about impact to queued workloads.
3) Ops runbook: 
   - 24h prior: create reservation in Dedicated control plane; notify infra team.
   - 2h prior: lock placement to avoid noisy neighbor scheduling.
   - If more than 50% of tranche is preempted for two consecutive days, auto-escalate to Capacity SR.

I've sketched a short runbook and uploaded it to the shared Drive link.

— Marcus
VP, Infrastructure

---

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@lumenrx.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2027 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary tranche shift for LumenRx pilot (autoscale exception + reservation ask)

Thanks all — LumenRx accepts the proposed time-sliced reservation (6 GPUs dedicated 14:00–18:00 PT; burst to 12 with preemption outside the window) and will sign the SLO amendment for the windowed reserved lane. We prefer the q3-llm-small-quant variant during test windows to keep costs predictable.

Couple of asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provide an ops contact to ping during the first three days of the pilot (Nov 29–Dec 1)?
- We'll need the reserved lane encoded in DocuSign for the SOW and to confirm billing terms.

Happy to move forward once we get a confirmation note and the DocuSign link.

— Priya Shah
Head of Infra, LumenRx

---

Summary/Next steps (internal):
- Kimberly/Marcus: implement time-sliced reservation and lower eviction scoring for Nov 29–Dec 19 (6 GPUs 14:00–18:00 PT, burst to 12). Confirm placement shard and impact window.
- Laura: draft SLO amendment + fallback runbook paragraph and link into DocuSign.
- Stephanie: share ops contact with Priya and confirm DocuSign link to LumenRx.

Deadline: internal confirmation to Sales by EOD Thu Nov 18 (for SOW cadence).
